description: A coding agent in the editor, in the spirit of Claude Code: it reads, edits and runs your project with your approval, using any Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible model, with skills, sub-agents, hooks and MCP tools.
untrusted: In Restricted Mode the agent does not read project instructions, skills, hooks or MCP servers from the workspace.

config.ai.title: AI Models
config.ai.endpoints: Model endpoints the agent can use. Add them with **AI: Add Model Endpoint**; API keys are stored in the OS keychain, not here.
config.ai.endpoints.name: A unique name, shown in the model picker.
config.ai.endpoints.provider.anthropic: The Anthropic Messages API (Claude), or a compatible gateway.
config.ai.endpoints.provider.openai: OpenAI-compatible chat completions: OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, Groq, DeepSeek, Mistral, Gemini, vLLM and others.
config.ai.endpoints.provider.copilot: GitHub Copilot: the models in your Copilot plan, after signing in with AI: Sign In to GitHub Copilot. The base URL is the GitHub API.
config.ai.endpoints.baseUrl: The API's base URL, for example https://api.anthropic.com or http://localhost:11434/v1.
config.ai.endpoints.models: Model IDs to offer from this endpoint.
config.ai.endpoints.contextWindow: How many tokens the models can read. Used for the context meter and automatic compaction.
config.ai.endpoints.maxOutputTokens: The most tokens to generate per response.
config.ai.endpoints.headers: Extra HTTP headers sent with every request.
config.ai.model: The model the agent uses, as `Endpoint name/model id`.
config.ai.monthlyLimit: Stop AI requests when this month's estimated spending reaches this many US dollars. `0` means no limit. You can allow more for the rest of a month when you reach it.
config.ai.prices: Your own prices for models, in US dollars per million tokens, by model id. A `*` matches any characters, for example `"my-company/*": { "input": 1, "output": 4 }`. These replace the built-in list prices used for **AI: Show Usage**.
config.ai.prices.input: US dollars per million input tokens.
config.ai.prices.output: US dollars per million output tokens.
config.ai.prices.cacheRead: US dollars per million input tokens read from the prompt cache. Defaults to a tenth of the input price.
config.ai.prices.cacheWrite: US dollars per million input tokens written to the prompt cache. Defaults to 1.25 times the input price.
config.agent.title: Agent
config.agent.permissionMode: What the agent may do without asking, in new conversations.
config.agent.permissionMode.default: Ask before edits: reads run freely; edits, commands and web requests ask first.
config.agent.permissionMode.acceptEdits: Auto-accept edits: edits inside the workspace run freely; commands ask first.
config.agent.permissionMode.plan: Plan: read only; the agent researches and proposes a plan for approval.
config.agent.permissionMode.bypassPermis: Full auto: everything runs without asking.
config.agent.permissions.allow: Tool calls that run without asking, written like Claude Code's rules: `Bash(npm test:*)`, `Bash(git status)`, `Edit(src/**)`, `WebFetch(domain:github.com)`, `mcp__github`.
config.agent.permissions.deny: Tool calls that are always blocked, in the same form as the allow rules, for example `Bash(git push:*)`.
config.agent.effort: How hard the model thinks, for models that support it (Claude Opus and Sonnet 4.6 and later, OpenAI reasoning models). Higher is slower and costs more.
config.agent.thinking: Show the model's reasoning, for models that support it.
config.agent.autoCompact: Summarize the conversation automatically when it nears the model's context window.
config.agent.checkpoints: Save a checkpoint of your files each time you send the agent a message, so you can take the code back to any earlier message (hover the **Checkpoint** line above it, or run **Agent: Restore Checkpoint...**). Checkpoints live in a separate Git store in Nighthawk's storage, never in your project's Git history. Files your `.gitignore` excludes, dependency folders such as `node_modules`, and new files over 25 MB are left out. Needs Git.
config.agent.maxSteps: The most model calls the agent makes for one message before it pauses.
config.agent.shell: The shell for commands. Empty picks bash (Git Bash on Windows), or PowerShell when bash is missing.
config.agent.systemPrompt: Extra instructions added to the agent's system prompt in every conversation.
config.agent.mcpServers: MCP servers whose tools the agent can use, in the `.mcp.json` format: `{ "github": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"] }, "docs": { "url": "https://example.com/mcp" } }`. Projects can also add a `.mcp.json`.
config.agent.hooks: Commands that run at points in the agent loop, in Claude Code's format: `{ "PostToolUse": [{ "matcher": "Edit|Write", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "npm run lint --silent" }] }] }`. Events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionStart.
view.background.welcome:
Give an agent a task to work on by itself while you keep coding. Each one gets its own Git worktree and branch, so agents never touch your files or each other. When one finishes, review its changes and merge them.
[Start Background Agent](command:nighthawk.agent.background.start)
config.agent.background.maxParallel: How many background agents work at the same time. More wait in a queue.
config.agent.background.permissionMode: What background agents may do without asking. Edits stay inside their own worktree either way.
config.inlineEdit.title: Inline Edit
config.inlineEdit.model: The model for inline edits (`Ctrl+I` in the editor), as `Endpoint name/model id`. Leave empty to use the agent's model. A fast model makes edits feel instant.
config.agent.memories: Let the agent save short facts it learns, such as your preferences or how this project builds, and read them in later conversations. Project memories stay with this workspace and are never written into it. Review them with **Agent: Show Memories...** or `/memories`.
config.agent.externalAgents: Other coding agents to run in the agent panel through the [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com), in addition to the built-in Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Codex. An entry with the same name replaces a built-in one. Start one with **Agent: New Conversation With...**. They run as programs on this computer with your permissions and their own sign-in.
config.agent.externalAgents.name: The name shown in the agent panel.
config.agent.externalAgents.command: The program to start, such as `npx` or the path to the agent.
config.agent.externalAgents.env: Extra environment variables for the agent, such as an API key it reads.
command.spec.revise: Ask for Changes to Spec Document
config.autocomplete.title: Autocomplete
config.autocomplete.enabled: Show AI suggestions as grey text while typing. `Tab` accepts a suggestion, `Ctrl+Right` accepts its next word, `Escape` hides it and `Alt+\` asks for one.
config.autocomplete.model: The model for autocomplete, as `Endpoint name/model id`. Leave empty to use the inline edit model (which falls back to the agent's). Pick a small, fast model: suggestions should appear within a second, and every pause in typing sends a request.
config.autocomplete.nextEdits: Predict your next edit from your recent ones, such as the next place a rename or a new parameter needs, where there is nothing to complete at the cursor. `Tab` jumps to the edit and `Tab` again accepts it. Uses the autocomplete model.
config.autocomplete.delay: How long typing must pause, in milliseconds, before a suggestion is requested. Longer waits send fewer requests.

view.scratches.welcome:
Scratch files are throwaway files of any language that live outside your projects. Every workspace sees them, and the play button runs them.
[New Scratch File](command:nighthawk.scratch.new)
config.scratch.title: Scratch Files
config.scratch.runners: Commands that run files, by extension, used by **Scratch: Run File**. `${file}` is the file and `${out}` a program a compiler writes; `&&` runs the next command when the one before worked. For example `{ "py": "uv run ${file}", "ts": "npx tsx ${file}" }`. Without one, a file runs with its `#!` line, else the usual command for its language (node, python3, go run, rustc, and so on).
command.macro.playTimes: Play Back Last Macro Several Times...
command.macro.playEachLine: Play Back Last Macro on Each Selected Line
config.index.title: Codebase Index
config.index.enabled: Index the workspace's code on this computer so the agent (its `CodebaseSearch` tool) and **AI: Search Codebase** can find code by meaning, such as "where do we handle sign-in?". The index follows `.gitignore`, `.nighthawkignore`, `.cursorignore` and `.aiignore`, and never includes files that usually hold secrets, such as `.env` and key files.
config.index.embeddingModel: The embedding model that lets the index find code by meaning, as `Endpoint name/model id` (for example `OpenAI/text-embedding-3-small`, or `nomic-embed-text` on a local Ollama). Leave empty to use one your endpoints offer: local ones right away, cloud ones after you agree. `off` finds code by words and names only, and sends nothing anywhere. Anthropic has no embedding models.
config.index.exclude: Glob patterns of more files and folders to leave out of the codebase index, such as `**/fixtures/**`.
config.index.maxFiles: The most files the codebase index holds per window.
config.autocomplete.disabledLanguages: Languages without autocomplete, by language id (for example `markdown`). Files that usually hold secrets, such as `.env` and key files, never get suggestions.
